plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Plush, ruffled blooms the size of teacups open from fat round buds. They give off a sweet, rosy perfume. The flowers arrive just as spring turns to summer, and they weigh down the stems with their petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring. Late-season cultivars typically peak in May and early June.
plants.location: Gardens across the central United States, such as St. Louis, Missouri, where late-season varieties bloom around late May
plants.funFact: Peonies are long-lived perennials. A single clump can bloom for decades, and some have outlasted the gardeners who planted them.

plants.name: Banksia
plants.description: Banksias carry tall, bottlebrush-like flower spikes made of hundreds of tiny blooms. In the cool Australian autumn, the spikes glow in the bush and draw honeyeaters and other nectar-feeding birds. Many species open from late summer through autumn and into winter, so late May falls in the middle of their flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn and winter, depending on the species
plants.location: Australia, where May is autumn in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: After flowering, banksia spikes turn into woody, knobbly cones. Many of them hold their seeds until a bushfire opens them.

plants.name: Rhododendron
plants.description: High in the Himalayan foothills, rhododendron shrubs and small trees cover the slopes in clusters of bell and funnel-shaped flowers. Some species bloom in May, so the mountain forests are still in color late in the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Varies by species and altitude. Several Sikkim species flower in May and June.
plants.location: Sikkim, in the eastern Himalaya of India
plants.funFact: Sikkim is home to a remarkable diversity of rhododendrons. Different species bloom at different elevations, so the flowering season shifts up the mountainside through spring and early summer.
